concepts.title: Work Done by a Force
concepts.body: Work is said to be done when a force acts on an object and displaces it in the direction of the force. The work done is calculated as the product of the force and the displacement in the direction of the force. For example, pushing a box across the floor involves doing work because the force applied moves the box.

concepts.title: Kinetic Energy and Potential Energy
concepts.body: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by an object due to its motion, while potential energy is the energy stored in an object due to its position or configuration. For instance, a moving car has kinetic energy, and a book placed on a shelf has potential energy due to its height above the ground.

concepts.title: Law of Conservation of Energy
concepts.body: The law of conservation of energy states that energy cannot be created or destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form to another. For example, when a pendulum swings, its potential energy converts to kinetic energy and vice versa, but the total energy remains constant.

formulas.title: Work Done
formulas.body: W = F x s (W in joule J, F in newton N, s in meter m). This formula calculates the work done when a force F displaces an object by a distance s in the direction of the force.

formulas.title: Kinetic Energy and Potential Energy
formulas.body: Kinetic energy = (1/2) m v^2 (m in kg, v in m/s). Potential energy = m g h (m in kg, g in m/s^2, h in m). These formulas are used to calculate the kinetic energy of a moving object and the potential energy of an object at a height h above the ground.

examples.title: Everyday Example
examples.body: When you lift a bucket of water from the ground to a table, you do work against gravity. The force you apply moves the bucket upward, and the work done is equal to the force multiplied by the height of the table.

examples.title: Applied Example
examples.body: A hydroelectric power plant converts the potential energy of water stored at a height into kinetic energy as it falls, which is then transformed into electrical energy. This process demonstrates the conversion of energy from one form to another.

mcqs.question: What is the unit of work?
mcqs.explanation: The unit of work is joule (J). Newton is the unit of force, watt is the unit of power, and pascal is the unit of pressure.

mcqs.question: A car of mass 1000 kg is moving at a speed of 20 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
mcqs.explanation: Using the formula KE = (1/2) m v^2, KE = (1/2) x 1000 x (20)^2 = 200000 J. The other options are incorrect because they do not match the calculated value.

mcqs.question: A ball of mass 2 kg is dropped from a height of 10 m. What is its potential energy just before it hits the ground? (g = 10 m/s^2)
mcqs.explanation: Using the formula PE = m g h, PE = 2 x 10 x 10 = 200 J. The other options are incorrect because they do not match the calculated value.
